figures.title: Which key/value head each query head reads
figures.caption: The three sharing schemes differ only in how many query heads share one key/value head: MHA gives each query head its own, GQA puts them in groups of four here, MQA gives all of them one. The entry is the KV head index; the cache scales with the number of distinct KV heads, not with query heads.
figures.alt: A grid of eight query heads down the rows and three schemes across the columns. The MHA column reads 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7: one KV head per query head. The GQA column reads 0,0,1,1,2,2,3,3: four groups, each shared by two query heads. The MQA column reads 0 in every row: one KV head for all query heads.

data.note: Schematic: 8 query heads and G = 4 shown. The chapter's model has 32 query heads; GQA with G = 8 puts four query heads in each group.

anim.intro: Switch the sharing scheme and watch the key/value heads collapse.

steps.label: MHA: every query head has its own key and value head, so the cache holds one KV head per query head.
GQA: query heads are divided into G groups, each with one KV head; G = 4 is shown.
MQA: a single KV head serves every query head.
The cache scales with distinct KV heads, so MQA pays one eighth of MHA on this schematic.

figures.title: The cache bill for one token at four sharing schemes
figures.caption: For 32 layers of 32 heads with d_head = 128 in FP16, the cache costs 512 KiB per token under MHA, 128 KiB under GQA with 8 groups, and 16 KiB under MQA: a 32x spread. MLA caches a 512-element latent plus a 64-element rotary key, 36 KiB per token, about 14.2x smaller than MHA.
figures.alt: Four horizontal bars in KiB per token across 32 layers. MHA is 512 KiB per token and 2 GiB at 4,096 tokens. GQA with 8 groups is 128 KiB per token and 512 MiB at 4,096. MQA is 16 KiB per token and 64 MiB at 4,096. MLA is 36 KiB per token and 144 MiB at 4,096.

data.note: 2 x 32 layers x g x 128 x 2 bytes. MQA reads 512 bytes per token per layer where MHA reads 16,384.

figures.title: MLA caches a latent, not per-head keys and values
figures.caption: MLA stores one 512-element latent plus a 64-element rotary key per token per layer: 576 elements, 1,152 bytes, 36 KiB across 32 layers. Each head reconstructs its own key and value from the latent with W_UK and W_UV, so nothing per-head is cached.
figures.alt: Three aligned panels. Panel one lists what is cached per token per layer: a 512-element latent, a 64-element rotary key, and 576 elements equal to 1,152 bytes in FP16, or 36 KiB across 32 layers. Panel two lists what each head reconstructs: k equals W_UK times the latent with d_head 128, v equals W_UV times the latent with d_head 128, and 32 heads share one 576-element cache. Panel three gives the bill at 4,096 tokens: 36 KiB per token, 144 MiB total, against 2 GiB for MHA.
